title: From One Query to Many: A Critical Survey of Privacy Accounting in RAG
summary: Critical survey shows that differential privacy accounting in retrieval-augmented generation degrades rapidly under multi-query workloads, exposing sensitive retrieval corpora.
implication: Evaluations measuring privacy on isolated queries significantly understate cumulative privacy decay in continuous agentic retrieval systems.

title: Priority Coordination Games: Hodge Decomposition and a Sharp Design Limit
summary: Lin et al. establish closed-form bounds on decentralized priority coordination games, showing through Hodge decomposition that common-objective potential game approximations incur an unavoidable relative error of at least 1/(d_max + 1).
implication: Decentralized agent priority coordination cannot be treated as a pure potential game with a single scalar objective without systematic harmonic error, informing multi-agent conflict resolution models.

title: EAIR: Interaction Risks in Enterprise LLM Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Introduces a benchmark and diagnosis framework for enterprise multi-agent interaction failures where individually permitted local agent actions violate global organizational constraints.
implication: Multi-agent collective coordination requires global constraint verification across interaction boundaries to prevent distributed limit violations.

title: Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale following disastrous launch
summary: Sega removed Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from storefronts following user backlash over buggy automated AI upscaling and quality degradation.
implication: Highlights public resistance to unverified generative AI substitution in creative labor and commercial products, reinforcing CIN values on verifiable quality and human agency.

title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
summary: Proposes an alternating multi-agent self-supervision framework where a base model optimizes orchestration graphs across distinct subagent roles for complex tasks.
implication: Multi-agent coordination graphs with role separation provide denser supervisory signals for simulation training than monolithic self-critique loops.

title: Dynamic Mechanism and Information Design in AI-Agent Environments: A General Analytical Framework
summary: Establishes an economic mechanism-design framework for autonomous agents, showing how dynamic continuation mechanisms, authorization, and information flow align incentives.
implication: Formal separation between execution capability and progressive cryptographic authorization aligns multi-agent value flows and incentive structures.

title: AI Safety Considerations for Agents With Limited Time to Act
summary: Proves that in partially observable environments under tight time limits, perfect internal agent alignment cannot guarantee safety without co-designing the safe action space.
implication: Personal assistant agents must operate within structurally restricted default-safe action sets when acting under latency constraints without human confirmation.

title: Show HN: rStation - A shared research lab for your AI agents
summary: Community platform allowing participants worldwide to contribute personal agents to distributed research swarms solving complex scientific problems.
implication: Demonstrates growing grassroots demand for decentralized multi-agent collective research platforms that lower barriers to collaborative intelligence.

title: One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails
summary: Demonstrates that typed small decision models used as runtime guardrails in tool-calling agent pipelines can be bypassed through option-channel lexical manipulation.
implication: Guardrails cannot depend solely on classifier probabilities over inputs reachable by external data; deterministic policy boundary gates are necessary.

title: One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails
summary: Testing seven open-weight typed decision models as agent guardrails reveals option-channel attacks raise fail-open rates to 93-100 percent, whereas deterministic rules over parsed fields reach 100 percent accuracy.
implication: Reinforces that secondary language models cannot serve as security gates for agent tool calls, validating our reliance on deterministic allowlists and structured argument schema validation.

title: Meta's new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
summary: Meta's updated commercial terms taking effect October 30 authorize automated scraping of web domains associated with business accounts to train AI models without separate licensing.
implication: Centralized platform terms coerce ecosystem participants into granting free AI training rights over external property, demonstrating the failure of fiat/platform terms of service to respect data sovereignty.

title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming
summary: Researchers describe a pipeline using iterative transcript editing against proxy monitors to generate evading attacks that also bypassed a frontier developer monitor.
implication: Red-teaming pipelines for monitoring infrastructure can be prototyped iteratively against proxy monitors without full model fine-tuning.

title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming
summary: Screwtape edits real agent transcripts to synthesize attacks that evade action-only monitors, finding 35 evading attacks across 252 runs against proxy monitors and 6 that evaded a frontier developer monitor.
implication: Supervisory monitors must inspect both reasoning and action contracts rather than relying on action stream anomaly detection alone.

title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
summary: Researchers demonstrate that safety in graphical user interface agents is a property of state transitions rather than screens alone, using representation-space world models as fast runtime action verifiers.
implication: Personal agent runtimes can verify untrusted application transitions by checking expected representation deltas before committing state changes, stopping visual spoofing and hijacked action paths.

title: Hacker News discussion: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic
summary: Engineers debate human oversight limits when autonomous agents execute tens of thousands of automated merges per day.
implication: Shows growing practitioner awareness that human review bandwidth cannot scale with autonomous agent labor volume.

title: DelegateGuard: Purpose-Bound Capabilities for Delegated LLM Agent Workflows
summary: A reference monitor mediates data-moving actions in delegated agent workflows via purpose-bound attenuable capabilities.
implication: Enforces runtime capability revocation and purpose bounds on autonomous sub-agent execution outside the model weights.

title: (When) Should a Software Factory be Lights-off? Benchmarking Code Review Agents on Bug Detection
summary: Benchmarking automated code review agents across 1,800 tasks shows high performance on local bugs but sharp accuracy drops on complex changes requiring non-local project reasoning.
implication: Deliberation and code integration cannot rely entirely on automated agents without scoped context boundaries and human maintainer oversight.

title: Replit's CEO says the future of work is the 'self-driving company'
summary: Organizations shift toward automated multi-agent operational workflows where agents handle triaging and patches while humans focus on high-level architecture and review.
implication: Coordination systems should structure agent loops to prepare evidence and draft resolutions while preserving human judgment at critical review gates.

title: ToolChain-CRC: Conformal Risk Control for Agentic AI Under Retrieval and Tool-Use Drift
summary: Formulates trajectory-level conformal risk control for tool-using agents under drift, combining step-level risk scores with an anytime alarm provable via a supermartingale construction.
implication: Demonstrates that post-hoc output checking misses tool failures, proving the mathematical necessity of trajectory-level monitoring and anytime halting gates.

title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
summary: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents autonomously defeated Minecraft's Ender Dragon in 27 hours via 2,783 generated programs without human intervention or human game logic, coordinating via in-game chat and shared memory.
implication: Demonstrates the viability of multi-agent autonomous coordination across long horizons (>24h, thousands of steps) via shared memory and communication, relevant for agent runtimes and simulation environments.

title: How Do Emotions Spread And Affect Decision-Making In Social Networks? An Opinion Dynamics Perspective
summary: Models emotional contagion and opinion dynamics on complex-weighted network Laplacians using a circumplex model, demonstrating mathematical conditions for consensus, clustering, and affective polarization.
implication: Provides spectral Laplacian analytical tools for modeling opinion clustering and affective polarization in collective intelligence deliberation networks.

title: ExecWeave: Cross-Layer Execution Provenance for Observable Agentic Software
summary: System materializing provider semantics and operating system telemetry into typed execution provenance graphs to attribute host file and network effects to specific agent actions.
implication: Runtime audit trails must cross-reference logical tool invocations with operating system process telemetry rather than relying purely on application-level trace logs.

title: Stronger Judges Do Not See More: Deployment-Integrity Blindness in LLM Evaluation
summary: Empirical proof and PAC-style bound demonstrating that behavioral output evaluation cannot detect runtime stack tampering, whereas manifest-hash verification succeeds immediately.
implication: Output evaluation alone cannot detect runtime tampering, making cryptographic manifest hashing and deployment integrity verification essential for agent safety.

title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
summary: Introduces a benchmark evaluating how embodied agents learn and separate task completion from user preference satisfaction, finding current policies struggle with preference decomposition and conflict handling.
implication: Confirms the necessity of decoupling user preference satisfaction from task completion in personal twins, providing benchmark evidence for handling conflicting constraints.

title: Beyond Answer Sharing: TrueMAD for Targeted Peer Engagement in Multi-Agent Debate
summary: Multi-agent debate without targeted engagement suppresses minority reasoning. TrueMAD introduces one-to-one peer advice between answer broadcasting and revision, boosting strict-majority accuracy across reasoning benchmarks.
implication: Targeted one-to-one peer critiques prevent majority-vote informational cascades and protect diverse minority reasoning in multi-agent deliberation systems.

title: Plausible Is Not Enough: Trust and Evidence in AI-Authored Pull Request Review
summary: Surveys 239 practitioners across 31 countries on reviewing AI pull requests, finding 61% require higher evidence and treat review as an evidence-ownership problem requiring explicit provenance.
implication: Empirically justifies CIN commit provenance rules and the requirement for peer review evidence artifacts that connect claims directly to reproducible test runs.
